title: Teacher expectancy and pupil IQ: 19 studies, standardized mean differences (Raudenbush 1984), dat.raudenbush1985
data_source: Raudenbush SW (2009). Analyzing effect sizes: random-effects models. In: Cooper H, Hedges LV, Valentine JC (eds), The Handbook of Research Synthesis and Meta-Analysis, 2nd ed., Russell Sage Foundation, pp. 295-315; Table 16.1 (p. 300). yi (standardized mean difference) and vi as listed at https://www.metafor-project.org/doku.php/analyses:raudenbush2009 (study 10 is 0.80, not the chapter's typo 0.87, cf. Raudenbush and Bryk 1985, Table 1).
notes: The effects are given as yi/vi, so this dataset validates SMD pooling (FE, DL, REML; Wald and Knapp-Hartung intervals), not the per-study SMD computation. Table 16.3 prints 3 decimals; the 4-decimal values are those the metafor test suite checks against Table 16.3 (tests/testthat/test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r, CRAN metafor). i2 is a proportion.

analyses.source: Raudenbush (2009), Table 16.2 (p. 301), p. 302 and Table 16.3 (p. 309), 'conventional' fixed-effects row, as checked in metafor's test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r; I^2 from the rma(method="EE") output at metafor-project.org analyses:raudenbush2009
